cover.title: Citizen Engagement in Public Space Development
body: We are inviting city officials and municipal planning professionals worldwide to share their experience with citizen engagement in public space development. Your answers will shape both the tool we are building and the upcoming Placemaking Trends 2026–2027 Report.
It takes about 7 minutes. All responses are confidential and reported only in aggregate. At the end you can opt in to receive the report, or to become an early adopter of the platform.
Thank you for contributing your expertise to building more inclusive, collaborative cities.
cover.glossaryTitle: You might need to know these words

glossary.definition: An approach to shaping the built environment in which residents, officials, and professionals jointly make decisions, rather than planning being done solely by experts on behalf of the public.
The ongoing process of informing, consulting, and involving local residents in decisions that affect their neighborhood or city.
A collaborative design method where end users actively help create a solution (a space, tool, or service) alongside designers, rather than simply being consulted or tested afterward.
Software that captures, stores, and visualizes spatial data on maps, allowing planners to analyze and layer information like land use, demographics, or infrastructure.

steps.module4Title: Module 4: Product concept and feature validation
steps.optInDescription: Your answers are ready to submit. If you would like the report, beta access or a demonstration, tick what applies and leave your details — all of it is optional, and Submit works without any of it.

module1.label: What best describes your primary role in the department?
What is the specific name of your role?
How long have you been working in that role?
Which municipality, city or country do you work in?
Which topic is your main operation area?
How high of a strategic priority is participatory urban design within your municipality's current long-term plan?

options.label: We don't have a long-term plan
We have a long-term plan, but it is not operational or not our sole focus
We have a long-term plan and it is operational

module1.label: How adequate is your department's annual budget allocation for civic engagement and public space co-design?

options.label: We have a budget, but it is not enough
We have a budget to work with, but more money would be better

module2.label: Do you have public participation software in your municipality?

options.label: We have one, but it is physical
We have one, and it is half physical, half digital
We have one, and it is fully digital

module2.label: Which digital tools do you currently rely on most for community engagement?

options.label: Spatial & GIS platforms: Maptionnaire, Felt, ArcGIS, etc.
Visual collaboration boards: Miro, Mural, Figma, etc.
Standard survey tools: Typeform, Google Forms, SurveyMonkey, etc.
Social & messaging channels: WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Groups, etc.
Custom / proprietary software: in-house or specialised municipal platforms

module2.label: How effectively do your existing digital tools meet your needs with regard to participatory urban design?
How accessible and intuitive is your city's current public participation software for non-technical citizens?

module3.label: What are your biggest challenges in placemaking?

options.label: Demographic reach: reaching diverse ages, online and in person
Data structuring: turning sticky notes and comments into GIS data
Visual communication: helping non-experts read complex 2D and 3D plans
Conflict resolution: navigating opposing views between stakeholder groups
Sustaining momentum: keeping residents engaged over long timelines
Executive buy-in: reports that convince councils and decision-makers
Resource limits: no budget or technical setup for custom tools
No case studies from other global cities

module3.label: How difficult is it for your department to convert qualitative citizen feedback into actionable steps?
What is, according to your opinion, the biggest challenge in participatory urban design processes?
module3.placeholder: Take as much space as you need.

module4.label: How valuable would a tool be that enables citizens and city staff to add, remove and filter visual ideas on an interactive map?
How useful would a searchable, peer-to-peer global repository of community-driven participatory urban design case studies be for your planning team?
How likely is your municipality to publish local case studies to an international digital participatory urban design network?
